title: Release binding and profile broadcast pipeline for model bundles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a CI/CD pipeline that produces immutable model release bundles, cryptographically binds model artifacts to a published performance profile, and broadcasts the resulting release metadata to the model registry and runtime catalog. This ticket covers: 1) build+pack: deterministic artifact creation (weights, tokenizer, metadata, provenance manifest), 2) credential signing: KMS-backed cryptographic signatures and SLSA-style provenance envelope, 3) profile binding: attach a published performance profile ID and quality metrics to the bundle in an auditable way, 4) staged rollout orchestration: publish release with cohort routing metadata and timeboxed automatic roll-forward, 5) observability hooks: emit release events and quality regressions to Console and QA dashboards, and 6) reconciliation: periodic job to detect drift between registry pins and runtime deployments and reconcile or create alerts. Success criteria: - Every release bundle created by the pipeline is content-addressable and has a signed provenance manifest. - The model registry contains a release record with a profile_id, signature, and rollout policy. - Runtime agents can atomically fetch a compatible bundle+profile and enforce fallbacks if the signature or profile check fails. - Unit and e2e tests for the pipeline and a smoke canary test that validates predictions against a golden testset before marking release as broadcasted.
comments: 2025-01-12 - Aisha Patel: Initial scoping complete. Chosen format: tar+zstd bundle with accompanying JSON-LD provenance manifest. We will use KMS asymmetric signing (RSA-4096) to match enterprise compliance. Blocking question: do we require hardware-backed keys for Hosted vs Private? Asked security for policy; added security_review_required=true.

2025-01-16 - Liang Chen: Prototype build step implemented (PR #104). Deterministic hashing validated for LLM weights on both float32 and int8 artifacts. Edge case: optimizer checkpoints cause non-determinism; resolved by stripping training-only metadata and normalizing float payload ordering.

2025-01-20 - Marco Ruiz (Security): Reviewed signing flow. Recommend HSM for private deployments and KMS for hosted. Added step to record key_id and key_type in provenance manifest. Also recommended rotating signing keys quarterly and including key rotation metadata in release record.

2025-01-24 - Erin O'Connor (PM): Requested that the pipeline attach a 'quality_gate' field derived from perf profile thresholds (latency P95 < 120ms, throughput >= 50 req/s for benchmark harness). Also asked for explicit rollback playbook to be embedded in the release metadata.

2025-01-28 - Liang Chen: Implemented profile binding logic. When a profile is published to the performance catalog it gets a profile_id (uuid). The pipeline will verify profile checksum and embed profile_id + min_acceptable_metrics in the bundle manifest. Added end-to-end test that fails release if the profile_id doesn't match the published profile registry.

2025-01-30 - QA (Sofia Martinez): Smoke canary test added to pipeline: deploy to ephemeral runtime slice, run 1k inference vectors against golden set, compute KL divergence and response similarity. Found a deterministic tokenization mismatch in older tokenizer v0.9.0; pipeline now asserts tokenizer version equality as part of the manifest.

2025-02-01 - Liang Chen: Added broadcast step that posts release events to the model registry, Console, and an internal slack channel #release-events. Implemented reconciliation job skeleton (cron) that compares registry pins to runtime deployed bundle digests and opens ENG tickets when drift detected (initially emits WARN for drift > 1 hour).

2025-02-02 - Aisha Patel: Design review with infra and runtime teams completed. Action items: - Add role-based gating: only maintainers and automation token can finalize broadcast. - Add feature flag to disable automatic broadcast for Private deployments. - Document emergency rollback steps in runbook (link added). Moving to In Progress for implementation sprint.
